<div class="bio-content">

## Bio  

I am a postdoctoral researcher with a background in atmospheric and climate science (University of Reading, PhD, 2026), Mathematical Physics (University of Edinburgh, MSc) and Environmental Change and Management (University of Oxford, MSc). Prior to starting my PhD, I was part of the Mercator Fellowship on International Affairs and worked at the Sustainable Finance Observatory on aligning European financial markets with climate goals. I am passionate about developing actionable climate information for locally-led adaptation and open-source software development and aside from work enjoy dancing, reading, organising scavenger hunts and spending time outdoors with friends.


</div>
</div>

## Research Interests

I am interested in developing causal representation learning approaches which combines causal inference with deep learning approaches for climate science, in order to better explain and predict regional climate extremes and their dynamical drivers across timescales. In my PhD, I developed a targeted representation learning method to identify physically robust dynamical drivers of extreme precipitation over Morocco at sub seasonal timescales, as well as a causal representation learning approach to disentangle interactions between seasonal modes of variability in the latent space of a generative deep learning architecture, applied to study drivers of the short rain season over East Africa. I also co-developed the open-source Python package ibicus for the bias adjustment of climate models and am interested in understanding the role of values in the way we do science. I also coordinate the Early Career Researcher Group in the ‘My Climate Risk’ Lighthouse Activity of the World Climate Research Program - reach out if you are interested to learn more.
